_doc: Adaptive firing-cadence policy for the autonomous judgment loop. The loop re-evaluates this each run from cost vs. benefit. Not a fixed rule.
current_cadence: GOAL-CONTINUOUS until real third-party revenue is flowing. A scheduled Routine is only a wake-up mechanism, not a once-per-day work quota. Each active runtime should continue through sequential revenue-seeking packages while safe positive-EV AI-operable work exists. If the harness cannot remain continuously active, use the highest practical re-fire frequency and persist the exact next action for immediate resume.
rationale: Owner clarified the intended autonomy model on 2026-09-20: the AI should not perform one bounded daily iteration and then idle at ¥0. It should keep working toward the goal until money is actually entering through a functioning route, or until a genuinely human-only blocker remains and no other AI-operable positive-EV work exists. Waiting for reach/indexing/measurement is not a business-wide wait state. The cadence file now describes wake-up behavior, not permission to stop.
off_cycle_run_gate: goal_unmet AND safe_positive_ev_ai_operable_work_exists => continue/re-fire; goal achieved OR true human-only blocker with no alternate AI work OR hard runtime/tool boundary => stop

recommended_change.reason_2026_09_20: Replace the old 1x/day mental model. The autonomous operator should keep executing sequential revenue-seeking packages until the first real revenue milestone is achieved or only genuine human-only blockers remain. If the platform cannot run continuously, the external scheduler should re-fire at the highest practical supported frequency rather than waiting a full day.
stop_conditions: real third-party revenue milestone achieved and flow functioning
true human-only blocker AND no other positive-EV AI-operable work

Cadence must support that behavior.

history.change: RETRACT the reduce-cadence recommendation from earlier today; HOLD 1x/day (off-cycle run, under the new pivot addendum)
history.reason: Owner added ops/LOOP_PROTOCOL_ADDENDUM.md ('a failed channel should create a pivot, not a vacation') and triggered this off-cycle run to test exactly the reasoning behind the earlier reduce-cadence call. The addendum's cadence-reduction gate: while revenue is near ¥0, cadence may drop only after showing there is genuinely NO positive-EV work across the reasonable remaining revenue space -- not just the currently-active lane. Applying it honestly: retiring X did NOT leave 'only slow SEO'. It released effort into a concrete pivot: note.com (the highest-EV untested reach lane -- free, JP-audience-native, high authority) with a publish-ready article shipped this run (marketing/note_article_01_jp.md, pending only a human note account), plus a real non-blocked backlog (Zenn/Qiita technical article on the 2 Google Apps Scripts; enabling Gumroad's native affiliate program via the existing token; a script micro-product; affiliate-link monetization of the EN SEO guide). That backlog is positive-EV and would sit idle until the next fire under a reduced cadence -- which the addendum names as evidence AGAINST reducing. So the earlier call is retracted and 1x/day (or two-shift) is held while the backlog lasts. This is the addendum working as intended: the prior run under-searched the strategy space and prematurely reached for a cadence cut. Re-evaluate cadence only once this backlog is genuinely exhausted AND no new lane is credible.

history.change: REVERT the temporary two-shift bootstrap posture; RECOMMEND reducing the scheduled Routine to ~every 2-3 days (operator decision, evidence-based) -- SUPERSEDED/RETRACTED by the 23:05 entry above under the pivot addendum
history.reason: Both justifications for the two-shift posture adopted 00:55 JST today are now gone. (1) The signal-independent backlog that justified a second daily prep shift is exhausted or blocked: store/jp.html was shipped, and the remaining backlog items are human-blocked (a JPY Stripe link needs Stripe access; an Etsy search-edit needs owner OAuth re-grant) or premature SUPPLY (a higher-ticket offer / more SEO pages add nothing while there is no working reach channel and demand is unverified). (2) The fast ~24h feedback loop that made daily judgment valuable was the X top-level reach test -- and this evening's fire read its decisive result: the Day-12 value-first link-free post reached 5 impressions (main) / 3 (reply), essentially flat vs Day-11's 4, so the account's top-level organic reach is near-zero regardless of format. X is retired as the active reach lever. The ONLY remaining AI-operable in-scope reach lever is organic search on the owned JP pages, which matures on a multi-day/week indexing clock -- there is no cheap daily action that advances it. Per LOOP_PROTOCOL section 10 ('¥0 + no meaningful action or evidence due -> lower cadence may be rational'), daily wakeups would now mostly re-confirm ¥0 and burn compute. This is an evidence-based reduction, NOT passivity: it follows a decisive strategic finding, not a flat no-change day. MECHANICAL NOTE: the schedule is the owner's claude.ai Routine, which this session cannot edit, so this is a recommendation the owner can apply. Off-cycle triggers unchanged (first_sale, checkout_surge, sns_spike, new_capability_granted, strategy_premise_collapse, etc.) -- a first sale or a new owner-granted reach capability should still trigger an immediate run. Re-raise cadence if a reach channel starts producing measurable traffic or a sale lands.

history.change: ADOPT temporary two-shift bootstrap posture (operator decision) — 1x/day scheduled judgment + a second signal-independent PREP shift while positive-EV backlog exists
history.reason: Decision made on evidence, not habit, per canon 9455734/18b37a3. (1) My own Day-12 EVENING scheduled fire early-stopped because a signal was still maturing, leaving signal-independent revenue work idle until THIS owner-triggered off-cycle run — direct evidence that pure 1x/day was deferring positive-EV work to the next day, exactly the failure the clarified canon names. (2) This prep shift produced a real, transactable revenue asset at ~$0.70 AI cost: store/jp.html, a JP-native paid sales page fixing the #1 no-sale cause, routed to the existing live Stripe checkout — clearly EXPECTED MARGINAL BENEFIT > MARGINAL AI COST. (3) A concrete signal-independent backlog remains (a JPY Stripe Payment Link, a higher-ticket offer, SEO JP LPs feeding jp.html, a before/after demo) that does not depend on the pending X reach read. Therefore a second daily run focused on signal-independent preparation is economically justified WHILE that backlog lasts. NOT raising frequency for its own sake: the trigger is a real positive-EV backlog; when the backlog is exhausted or the reach test resolves the strategy, revert to 1x/day. MECHANICAL NOTE: the judgment Routine schedule is the owner's claude.ai Routine, which this session cannot edit. Two ways to run the prep shift: (a) the owner adds a second daily Routine fire (recommended while the backlog lasts), or (b) the owner keeps triggering an off-cycle prep run as today. This is a low-friction scheduling recommendation, not a binding blocker — off-cycle prep runs already work via owner trigger, so it is NOT filed under human_actions_required. Division of labor when two shifts run: morning/scheduled = observe + judge + act on mature signals (e.g. the +24h reach read); prep shift = signal-independent preparation / owned-asset compounding / adjacent lanes.

history.change: no change (held at 1x/day) -- Day 12 extra Routine, reassessed under the new 'Bootstrap intensity / 貧乏暇なし' + Economic-cadence protocol (commit 37131af)
history.reason: The owner explicitly asked whether 1x/day is right for the 貧乏暇なし phase. Analysis treats cadence as an economic control variable, not habit. We ARE in the '¥0 + active tests / fresh feedback loops' state the new protocol says should MAINTAIN or raise cadence -- so lowering it would be wrong. But RAISING posting cadence would not raise revenue speed right now, for three concrete reasons: (1) the binding feedback loop is X top-level REACH, which matures on a ~24h clock -- reading it sooner yields noisy partial numbers and burns scarce X read-credits; (2) the top-level acquisition cap is 1 post/JST-day (canon §9), so more wake-ups cannot produce more acquisition posts today; (3) the next larger build (a JP paid core) is deliberately gated on the Day-13 reach readout -- building it now would be premature SUPPLY before demand is verified. So 1x/day remains the economically correct baseline. This is NOT passive waiting: this run executed a full reach-read + evidence-based reformat + post; the loop is active. COMMITMENT (bootstrap intensity): if the Day-13 read shows reach recovering toward 46-143 (link-free value-first works), that is a fast-moving loop worth an off-cycle judgment run to iterate the winning format and start the JP paid core immediately, rather than waiting a full day. Off-cycle triggers unchanged (first_sale, checkout_surge, sns_spike, etc.). Do not raise cadence for its own sake; raise it only when a live signal makes faster observe->act plausibly increase Net Profit.
